The product bound gives \(\rho_\lambda\ge\sqrt{\beta(\lambda)}\), and choosing \(r\lambda=1+\beta(\lambda)\) attains equality. Direct replay of the source state equations and characteristic roots from the packaged verifier agrees with every formula.

value.rationale: The derivative channel is the defining addition that distinguishes the optimizer from ordinary momentum and is explicitly motivated as an overshoot-damping mechanism. On the canonical fixed-Hessian model, the exact algebra shows that this channel becomes positive curvature-dependent momentum and imposes a hard gain ceiling independent of the learning rate. The exact best modal rate floor and loss-rescaling instability sharpen the interpretation: increasing derivative gain raises an irreducible asymptotic rate floor and can make a mere positive rescaling of the loss impossible to stabilize. This is a structural optimizer calibration result rather than a routine parameter substitution.
